method: Both reviewers read every German string of the current file (mtime 2026-09-28 01:04, after r2 at 00:42): title and title.canDo, spec.situation and spec.deviation, the Folge (8 lines, gist item), the LS1 and LS2 dialogues (10 lines each), the LS3 chat, the 5 exam texts (10 ads), the strategy card, every promptDe, option, tile, accepted form and explanation.de, the three micro-outputs, both aussprache blocks, the Sp2 and Sp3 parts (instructions, situations, cards, aiRole, openingLine, 8 hintWords, 16 model turns), the S2 task (situation, taskDe, 3 Leitpunkte with cues, checklist, model text), 8 Redemittel with their function labels, the check line, every endLine, the story beat and cliffhanger, the rule cards rc.akkusativ, rc.kein and rc.negation-nicht, and the five registry can-do texts of start.lernziele as the player shows them. We solved all 94 items blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line, never from promptEn or the key (Folge gist 1; inputItems 3 × 5; structuredInput 3 × 4; pool 11 + 11 + 12; reserve 4 + 5 + 5; LS3 perception 4; L2 5; Check 8; proof 1). Every sentence_building item was permuted against its frame, every error_correction was solved for every correct correction under its named category, and every determiner cue ((der), (ein), (kein), (mein), (dein)) was checked against the noun's plural. We ran 93 candidate answers through the real grader, src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js (validator.grader). We ran a stem-overlap and option-shape baseline over all 33 choice items with three options (unique maximum overlap of key with stem, only option with a different first word, key ≥ 1.5 × the length of every distractor). Exam blocks were checked against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json (l2: 5 items, a/b, 9–26 words per ad; sp2: 2 topics, cards-ask; sp3: 2 rounds, cards-request, an information question is sent back, textVariantDe for word cards; s2: 3 Leitpunkte, about 30 words, Anrede and Gruß scored as text type, never as a Leitpunkt). For lexis and grammar we used a walker on the validator's own machinery (lexicon.mjs knownForms + licensedForms at a1.1-u06, metalanguage.mjs, compounds.mjs, detectors.mjs detectInText with the full lexicon env, spine.mjs detectorPlacement) over all 543 German strings of the unit, including surfaces LEX-01 and GRM-04 do not read, over the five Lernziele texts, and over every German wording proposed below. A second walker compared every production surface (model sentences, Redemittel, hintWords, learner cards and model turns, writing cues, checklist, model text, read-aloud lines) against the lemma roles in a1.1/lexicon.json. Sentence lengths of all Folge, input, model-turn and model-text sentences of a1.1 u01–u12 were measured with lib-validate/text.mjs wordCount against level-profiles.json (a1.1 sentence.maxWords 12, meanWordsMax 7, subordinateClausesMax 0). Cast and story were checked against casts/series.json and casts/a1.json, the u05 cliffhanger and the u07 Folge and LS1. Owner files were checked for changes since r2 by mtime: registries/cando/a1.json, lib/compiler.mjs, rule-cards.json, lexicon.json, grammar-spine.json, SCHEMA.md, lib/schemas/common.mjs, every rules/*.mjs and checkItem.js all predate r2. Every proposed unit edit was applied to a scratch copy in the session scratchpad and validated there (validator.scratch).

findings.quote: ls1-p04 „Olena sucht ___ Schlüssel. (der)“ → accepted [„den“] · ls1-l10 Frau Schulz: „Ja, genau: der Schlüssel, die Schlüssel.“ · grader: „die“ → wrong, errorTag case-np
findings.problem:
r1-F04 closed the (mein) and (kein) cues before nouns whose plural looks like the singular, and r2 verified the (ein) cues. The (der) cue was not checked. Its plural form „die“ is also correct here: „Olena sucht die Schlüssel.“ is standard German. LS1 teaches exactly this plural one screen earlier (ls1-l10). Only promptEn („der → accusative form“) and the explanation fix the number. The grader marks „die“ WRONG and sends the learner to the case-np repair card for a case error they did not make.
(der) points to the singular more strongly than (mein) did. „die“ is a form of the article der, just as „meine“ is a form of mein, but many learners hear it as a different article. So this is MINOR rather than r1-F04's MAJOR. It is the last instance of that class in the unit: every other (der) cue stands before Kuli or Laptop, whose plurals differ, and Kalender, Drucker and Computer carry (ein) or fixed options.
findings.fix:
ls1-p04:
- promptDe: „Olena sucht ___ Bleistift. (der)“
- explanation.de: „der Bleistift → den Bleistift. Nach „suchen“ steht der Akkusativ.“
- explanation.en: “der Bleistift → den Bleistift: accusative after suchen.”
